adjustments: disallowed dependency exemptions for T.G., S.G., O.G.
disallowed child tax credits including refundable portion
disallowed earned income tax credit (portion attributable to the children)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Dependency exemptions, CTC/ACTC and EITC for niece and nephews
conceded: Respondent conceded before trial that petitioner is not liable for the 6662(a) penalty
Respondent conceded children satisfied relationship, age and support tests
Respondent conceded entitlement to some of the EITC (disputing only portion attributable to the children)

findings_of_fact.fact: Children T.G. born 2000, S.G. born 2007, O.G. born 2010; ages 15, 8, 5 at end of 2015 (derived)
findings_of_fact.snippet: T.G., born in 2000, S.G, born in 2007, and O.G., born in 2010.

findings_of_fact.fact: Children are niece and nephews (children of petitioner's brother Thomas Griffin, a disabled single parent)
findings_of_fact.snippet: Their father, Thomas Griffin, was a single parent and disabled.

findings_of_fact.fact: Children stayed overnight with petitioner from last two weeks of May to mid-August, weekends, school closures, holidays; school nights with father
findings_of_fact.snippet: stayed overnight with petitioner from the last two weeks of May to mid-August. They also stayed overnight with petitioner during weekends, school closures, and holidays

findings_of_fact.fact: Court found children resided with petitioner more than one-half of 2015 (credibility finding)
findings_of_fact.snippet: we find it more likely than not that the children resided with petitioner for more than one-half of 2015.

findings_of_fact.fact: Brother signed Form 8332 during exam; not attached to return; given less weight
findings_of_fact.snippet: However, petitioner did not attach the signed form to her 2015 income tax return.

findings_of_fact.fact: None of the children attained age 17 during 2015
findings_of_fact.snippet: None of the children attained the age of 17 during 2015.

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to dependency exemption deductions for T.G., S.G., and O.G. for 2015?
issues.holding: Yes; residency test met on credible testimony; relationship, age, support conceded
issues.computable_reason: Residency (> half year) found from credibility of testimony; months not quantified. Other tests mechanical given that finding.

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to child tax credits (including additional child tax credits) for the three children?
issues.computable_reason: Given qualifying-child finding (I1), under-17 test is mechanical from birth years

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to the EITC portion attributable to the three children?
issues.holding: Yes; entitled to EITC as claimed
issues.computable_reason: Follows from qualifying-child finding in I1; EIC amount not stated

decision.text: Decision will be entered for petitioner.
decision.summary: Dependency exemptions, CTC/ACTC and EITC allowed for all three children; penalty conceded by respondent

notes: Case decided on preponderance of evidence; residency turned on credibility (school calendar corroboration). Income amounts not stated. Some facts stipulated.
